Vs.

full_judgment: 12. It appears that the High Court Division has considered this point seriously and examined the application filed by the writ petitioner before the Managing Director of the Biman praying for rescinding his dismissal order the annexure-R and has opined that though the caption of  that application did not state the word "appeal" but for all practical purposes this application was filed by way of appeal after the order of dismissal  and that merely an omission to write the words "appeal" under regulation 59 could not make the said application a barren one. The High Court Division held that application was an appeal and the contents and prayers made in that appeal ought to have been considered by the concerned authorities under regulation 59 itself. We are fully in agreement with the above observations and finding of the High Court Division. After the impugned dismissal order the writ petitioner filed the above mentioned application to the Managing Director of Biman-who was the appellate authority-within the statutory period of limitation as prescribed by clause (4) of regulation 59 of the Regulations 1979 praying for rescinding his dismissal order. There can be no reason for not treating this application as an appeal under Regulation 59. The mere omission to write the word appeal in this application cannot be aground for not treating this application as an appeal. The authority concerned ought to have treated this application of the writ petitioner as an appeal. However, since this writ petitioner applied to the appellate authority for rescinding his dismissal order within the time prescribed by the service regulation but did not get any result within a considerable time the writ petition cannot be said to be not maintainable.
